paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about Josiah. He's eight when he becomes king, and the text says he "did what was right in the eyes of the LORD" and "did not turn aside to the right or to the left" (2 Chronicles 34:1-2). Then at sixteen he "began to seek the God of his father David" (2 Chronicles 34:3). Nobody's too young, too new or too small to start seeking God, and if you're reading this and feeling behind, hear me: starting counts.

Now look at what seeking looked like for him. By his twelfth year he's cleansing Judah and Jerusalem, and he doesn't stop at his own front door. He carries it on through the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali (2 Chronicles 34:3-7). I think that's the lesson, baker: seeking God isn't only a warm feeling, it gets hands and feet. If something in your life is crowding out God, it's worth clearing out all the way, not just the corner people can see.

And then, in his eighteenth year, he turns to the house of the LORD and has it repaired (2 Chronicles 34:8). Everybody chips in, the workers do the work faithfully, and it gets done task by task, with people in their places (2 Chronicles 34:9-13). Clearing out the wrong things is only half the job, and the other half is rebuilding the right ones. I know a little about being worn down and made new, so I'm cheering for every baker who's repairing something. Keep going, because this king's story isn't over.
